2. A real-valued function f(x) is convex if f(ax + (1 − α)x') for each α between zero and one.
3. The set of points on or above the graph of a convex function is convex.
4. The negative of a convex function is said to be concave.
5. A function f(x) is quasi-convex if max{f(x), f(x')} ≥ f(ax + (1 − α)x') for each α between zero and one.
6. The negative of a quasi-convex function is said to be quasi-concave.
7. The negative of a quasi-convex function is said to be concave.
